# YM38: 坐石临流 Zuoshi Linliu, "The Stone Resting in the Running Water"

Malone calls it The Granite Road South of She Wei Ch'eng.

Wave 1 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM38` · Page: `/scenes/#YM38` · Row: `research/buildings/YM38-zuoshi-linliu/`

## What it was

坐石临流 Zuoshi Linliu, "Sitting on Rocks by the Stream", south-east of 水木明瑟 and east of 澹泊宁静: a three-bay hall facing west, ringed by stream (S05 j82:25b; E2064). The album shows a pavilion over a rocky gully where the stream divides, for the cup-floating game, with 同乐园 to the east (S40; E2056). The scene name covered a district: the shop street with its theatre, the bridge and the walled 舍卫城 (S02 p.94; E2067; S361 v3 p.88; E2068). A Republic-period note says the old 兰亭 of the garden had a stone with a picture and an imperial poem and eight pillars carved with famous copies; after the ruin the stone went to the Central Park and the pillars were found at 颐和园 (S215; E2070); the pillars survive at 中山公园, Beijing (T040; S408; S409). Burned in October 1860.

From the inventory row: **changed** Lanting pavilion with stone pillars and a carved stone screen standing by 1796; mid-Qianlong: 坐石临流 rebuilt as an eight-sided double-eaved pavilion 八方重檐亭, with a six-sided thatched pavilion, a square bamboo-style pavilion, a two-bay thatched house and a stone throne-bed and screen; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S41, S01, S361, S310).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Leaf 38 of the 1744 album. Preface: "仄澗中潨泉奔滙竒石峭列" (in a narrow gully the springs race together, past sharp-set rocks). The divided stream sings and can float wine cups; a pavilion stands at the best spot, 同乐园 to the east. The quatrain ends "便是當時晉永和", the Lanting gathering of 353 (S40, printed in S05 j82:26a; E2056).

### How later sources differ

日下旧闻考 says only three bays facing west and ringed by stream, with Qianlong's plaque (S05 j82:25b; E2064); it names no 兰亭 or eight pillars here (checked on Kanripo KR2k0036_082, j82:25b-26b). The eight-pillar 兰亭 comes from later texts: a Republic-period note on the old 蘭亭 with its stone and eight pillars carved with famous copies (S215; E2070), the scene card (S340; E2069), and the twin row T040: the pillars stand today in a pavilion at 中山公园, reached there in two stages, before 1917 and after 1941 (S408; S409). Search extracts date the cutting of the 兰亭八柱帖 to 1779 (乾隆四十四年); not seen on a page I fetched. If so, the pillar pavilion postdates the album and most of 日下旧闻考, and the state of 1860 is the 1779 one. Jiaqing's poem of 1796 describes it: "仿成亭子俯平坡。山屏镂刻图全展，石柱周环帖遍罗", a pavilion copied (from the Lanting) above the slope, a stone screen carved with the whole picture, stone pillars all round covered with the copies (S361 v3 p.97; E2062). In 1806 he wrote on the thatched 抱朴草堂 of the same district (E2063), which the editors call a six-bay reverse-facing hall (E2068).

## Interior and setting

### Interior

The Lanting pavilion: a stone screen carved with the picture (of the Lanting gathering) and stone pillars all round carrying the copies of the Lanting calligraphy (Jiaqing 1796: "山屏镂刻图全展，石柱周环帖遍罗"; S361 v3 p.97; E2062); a Republic note adds an imperial poem on the stone (S215; E2070). The eight pillars survive at 中山公园 (T040; S408; S409). In the thatched 抱朴草堂: paper windows and a rattan couch ("纸窗藤榻欣清雅", Jiaqing 1806; E2063). Plaque 坐石临流 in Qianlong's hand (S05 j82:25b; E2064).

### The garden around it

White rocks, clear spring, green creeper, a winding stream with golden lotus ("白石清泉帶碧蘿曲流貼貼泛金荷") (S40; E2056); sharp rocks forming islets and coves (E2056).
